newsitem.title: CHINA: China to build $700 mln pulp mill in Guangdong.
newsitem.headline: China to build $700 mln pulp mill in Guangdong.

text.p: China will build a $700 million pulp mill in a project which officials have called a turning point in the nation's paper industry, the official Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

The mill, designed to have a capacity of 300,000 tonnes a year, would be built in Zhanjiang in the southern province of Guangdong, the agency said, quoting an agreement between the Ministry of Forestry and the provincial government.
The project would be the largest of its kind in the country, marking a turning point in China's ancient paper-making industry, it said in a report late on Thursday.
The agency quoted Vice-Minister of Forestry Li Yucai as saying that China's production of paper-making raw materials had long been too low to meet demand.
In 1995, China spent $2.68 billion importing pulp and pulp products but also exported large quantities of wood, Xinhua said.
The new Zhanjiang mill would be located close to reserves of high quality forests, it said without giving details of when construction would begin or be completed.
